gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Capture It stands tall and flat-lined, like fineliner on paper. Noto Sans Oriya, with its generous curves and near-capital-height lowercase, gives that tight display heading a loosened, friendly counterweight.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-palmy: Chunky outlines, towering letters, and Capture It makes a tight, urban statement. Noto Sans Palmyrene runs in clean, modern lines whose curves stop short of closing, so a long paragraph keeps breathing.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-pau-c: Blunt, towering and unshaded, Capture It has no calligraphic tricks. Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau keeps its curves open and its lowercase close to cap height, so paragraphs read smoothly.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-siddh: Closed, stout and stubbornly uniform, Capture It looks cut from one stroke. Noto Sans Siddham, with its large lowercase band and wide-swinging s, makes a long paragraph feel open and easy going.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-soyom: A towering x-height gives Capture It its urban, commanding stance. Noto Sans Soyombo below shares that tall lowercase but opens its curves wide, so the two sit together easily.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-sunuw: Stiff, sealed-up and tall, Capture It has no hairlines to soften it. Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in every curve, like a rope's open bight, with short ascender stems rising from tall lowercase bodies.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-syria: Capture It is closed up tight and tall, made for big, brief lines. Noto Sans Syriac blows its tall lowercase bowls round like glass bulbs and turns its s shapes wide and easy.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tagal: Bent-tubing letters, towering and nearly sealed: that is Capture It. Noto Sans Tagalog supplies the opposite, a dominant middle zone with generous gaps in every curve, and that open-versus-closed tension carries the pair.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tai-l: A towering x-height and nearly sealed letters define Capture It. Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its strokes out before they touch and barely steps from cap to lowercase, which loosens things beneath.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified, its terminals stopping far from the stem. Beneath Capture It, whose strokes run identical in weight both ways, a long paragraph reads smoothly and feels contemporary.
